title: Your AI Agent Needs a Kill Switch
topic: How software founders can control AI agents before granting write access
audience: software founders adding AI agents to real business workflows

narrative.hook: Your AI agent does not need more freedom. It needs a clear way to stop
narrative.problem: Teams connect agents to email, customer data, or production tools, then judge them by a successful demo
narrative.stakes: But the real test is a vague instruction, bad data, or an action that costs money
narrative.reframe: So before you add another ability, give the workflow three simple controls
steps: define what it may read, what it may change, and how much it may spend
require a person to approve actions that reach a customer, move money, or delete data
keep a receipt showing the input, decision, action, result, and person who approved it

proof.statement: run one bad-input test. If the agent pauses, explains the problem, and leaves a useful receipt, your controls are working

narrative.takeaway: A trustworthy agent is not one that never fails. It is one that fails visibly and can be stopped

cta.text: Book an AI Automation Audit to map one risky workflow before you use it with write access
